newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton ends lower, trade sells on close.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton ends lower, trade sells on close.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures closed lower as trade selling in new-crop December drove prices to session lows just ahead of the close, floor sources said.
"The weather is fine and the crop looks good," a floor source said.
USDA will release its weekly crop progress report today amid expectations that the 1997/98 cotton crop is developing on schedule.
December settled at 74.93 cents a lb, down 1.09 cents, after trading from 76.25 to 74.80 cents. Spot July fell 0.91 cent to 72.24 cents, while the rest finished 0.78 to 1.03 lower.

Analysts said the market is not likely to retrace losses amid a lack of fundamental news before the official planted area estimate, released on June 30. The estimate is expected to prompt a revision in the July supply and demand numbers, analysts said.

"The market's recent stability based on balanced supply and demand is vulnerable to any sizable shortfall in production," Carl Anderson, a cotton marketing specialist with Texas A&M University, said in a weekly market comment.
He said many industry sources expect planted area to total about 14 million acres, which "would barely produce enough cotton for the expected use."
But the world cotton supply will need to fall substantially for December futures to pierce 78.00 cents, where firm resistance has been pegged.
Volume was estimated at 15,000 lots compared with Friday's official 10,897 lots.
